title: Check-in plan
description: What the caretaker intends to find out across the interval a consultation opened, written once when the visit is summarised rather than improvised call by call. This is deliberately a plan and not a script: it fixes the agenda — which commitments and which clinical patterns are worth pursuing, and from which week — while leaving the wording, the ordering and the follow-ups to the agent on the call. Persisting it is what makes the interval auditable ahead of time rather than only in hindsight: the brief can report what was planned against what was actually asked, and a plan that never got covered is itself a finding.

tracked_symptoms.description: The symptoms to score 1-10 on every call, chosen once from what the consultation raised and what the disease context says changes over this interval. Their wording is frozen here and reproduced verbatim by the agent on every call — the one place in this system the agent does not phrase things itself. That is the whole mechanism: a score is comparable with last month's score only if the question, the scale and the anchors were identical, so a reworded question silently breaks the series. Keep the set small; each one costs a turn on every call, and a patient asked six numbers stops giving considered ones. Empty is correct when the consultation raised nothing with a severity worth tracking.

id.description: Stable slug keying this series across every call of the interval, e.g. "tiredness".

label.description: Short name for a brief line or a chart axis, e.g. "Tiredness".

question.description: The question, in the patient's own register, asked verbatim every call. Phrase it so 10 is the worst end on every tracker — ask about tiredness, not about energy — because the scale direction is fixed system-wide and a reversed item would be read the wrong way round. Do not include the scale anchors; they are appended identically to every tracker.

context_id.description: The check_in_probe, trajectory marker or red_flag id that justifies tracking this. "" only when it comes purely from what the patient described at the consultation.

from_consultation.description: True when the patient actually raised this at the appointment. A symptom they described themselves is the one they will answer thoughtfully about for months; one drawn only from the guideline is worth tracking but is a colder question.

interval_goal.description: One sentence on what this interval has to establish before the next appointment, in plain language. The agent reads this to know what the call is ultimately for when the specific items run out.

reasoning.description: Why this agenda for this patient — what in the visit or the clinical context shaped it. The audit trail for the plan itself, as `reasoning` is for a single turn.

items.description: The agenda. Ordered by priority, most important first.

id.description: Stable slug for this agenda item, e.g. "blood_test_done". Reused as a `covers` value so turns can be matched back to the plan.

intent.description: What this item is trying to establish, stated as an aim rather than as a question to read aloud — e.g. "whether the repeat blood test has actually happened". The agent phrases it itself.

why.description: Why it matters in this interval, grounded in the visit or the disease context. Never a clinical conclusion.

from_week.description: The earliest week this is worth asking. Asking about a seven-week blood test in week one wastes a question on a patient whose scarcest resource is attention.

from_day.description: The earliest day this is worth asking, for items that belong to the day-after first contact rather than to a week of the interval — collection, first dose, the daily reminder time, anything unclear from the consultation. Takes precedence over from_week when set, so a first-contact item is due on day 1 without becoming due for every later call in week 0.

until_week.description: After this week the item stops being worth asking, or null if it stands for the whole interval.

priority.description: 1 is must-ask on every eligible call, 3 is ask if there is room. The turn budget is small and fatigue is a symptom of this population, so most calls will not reach priority 3.

ask_directly.description: True when an open question will not surface this and it must be asked about by name. Set for patterns the patient would never connect to their condition and so will never volunteer — the highest-value catches are all of this kind.

commitment_ids.description: Commitments from the visit this item tracks. Empty when it pursues a clinical pattern rather than something the patient agreed to.

context_ids.description: Ids from the disease context this item derives from — red_flags, trajectory, monitoring or check_in_probes. Every item should cite at least one unless it comes purely from what was said at the visit.

call_schedule.description: When to call across the interval, and what each call is mainly for. Weeks are relative to the visit date. The first entry should almost always be the day-after first contact (week 0, day 1), which confirms the plan is real and workable before any of the rest of the interval depends on it.

week.description: Weeks after the visit. 0 is the week of the consultation itself, which is when the day-after first contact falls; use `day` to place a call inside it.

day.description: Days after the visit, when a call needs finer placement than a week — the day-after first contact is day 1, and an early adherence check is around day 5. Null means the call sits anywhere in its week.

focus.description: What this particular call is for, in one phrase.

item_ids.description: Agenda items intended for this call.
